rule: One server clock (+1 per 100 ms) is broadcast about every 2 s; the client keeps its own counter and slews to it (snap at a 10-tick gap, else one tick per packet). Phase = tick mod cycle. Ambient is a scalar that holds a night floor. Sky colour is a per-channel staged ramp on solar presence (dusk uses 1 minus progress), so blue leaves first at dusk and red last. Biome fog eases to its target with t = 1 - exp(-2 dt), then the fog colour is multiplied by the sky factor. The night tint is a per-channel floor (max with the scalar ambient).
keep: One server clock; clients slew toward it and snap on a large gap
Phase from clock modulo cycle, with progress inside each phase
Ambient scalar with a floor at night and eased ramps at dusk and dawn
Per-channel staged sky ramp: blue leaves first at dusk, red last; reverse at dawn
Eased fog blend on biome change, frame-rate independent via exp smoothing
Fog colour multiplied by the sky factor so the horizon matches the sky
change: Donor draws no sun disc (TODO at renderer.zig:156); we draw a sun or moon sprite
Duels never blend fog or sky; the zone preset is read as it was at engage
Phase split and durations become zone data, not code constants
Night tint is set in our palette; no donor colour values
look_test: Preview-only flag on the 3-attacker Pit arena with a 4-stop time slider (dawn, noon, dusk, night) and a fixed sky preset; publish to /preview/ with no release rows. Compare noon and night stills at the fight camera at 375 wide. Dom checks that three attackers stay separable at night, that dusk reads as dusk not damage tint, and that night is dim not black.
